title: National Income: GDP, GNP, and Measuring an Economy

questions.question: GDP is defined as the market value of all final goods and services produced:
options: By a country's residents anywhere in the world
Within a country's domestic territory in a year
questions.rationale: GDP counts production inside the domestic territory regardless of who produces it; GNP instead counts production by residents.

questions.question: The expenditure method expresses GDP as:
options: Sum of value added by all firms
questions.rationale: Final spending equals consumption plus investment plus government spending plus net exports — the expenditure identity.

questions.question: GNP equals GDP plus:
questions.rationale: GNP adjusts domestic output by NFIA — residents' earnings from abroad minus non-residents' earnings domestically.

questions.question: For India, net factor income from abroad is negative. This means:
questions.rationale: Income repatriated by foreign investors in India exceeds Indian earnings abroad, so subtracting a negative NFIA makes GNP slightly lower than GDP.

questions.question: Why are intermediate goods excluded from GDP?
options: To avoid double counting their value
They are counted in GNP instead
questions.rationale: The value of bread already includes the value of the flour; counting both would double count — hence the value-added approach.

questions.question: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP is valued at:
questions.rationale: Real GDP uses base-year prices (2011-12 in India's national accounts), so it changes only when physical output changes.

questions.question: If nominal GDP is ₹110 lakh crore and real GDP is ₹100 lakh crore, the GDP deflator is:
questions.rationale: Deflator = (Nominal ÷ Real) × 100 = 1.10 × 100 = 110, indicating prices 10% above the base year.

questions.question: In the circular flow, which of the following is a leakage?
questions.rationale: Leakages — savings, taxes, imports — drain spending from the domestic flow; injections — investment, government spending, exports — refill it.

questions.question: The Human Development Index, published by UNDP since 1990, uses which three dimensions?
options: Health, education, and standard of living
questions.rationale: HDI combines life expectancy, years of schooling, and per-capita GNI (log-scaled) to capture welfare beyond raw output.

questions.question: Which of these is a recognised limitation of GDP as a welfare measure?
options: It ignores non-market household work and environmental damage
It is measured only every decade
questions.rationale: GDP misses home production, the underground economy, distribution, and depletion of nature — the lesson's table of limitations.
